comparison: Both evaluations support claims about BEHAV3D-TP's design, capabilities, and accessibility (C4, C5, C22-C24, C68, C71-C72, C79-C80). Peer review includes C69-C70 (Google Colab implementation) which OpenEval addresses separately in R19. Both affirm the tool's utility and user-friendliness with solid evidence of multi-format compatibility.

Perfect agreement on breast cancer and TEB dataset validation (C26-C31). Both evaluations confirm results are consistent with original studies and provide additional insights. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative results and figure support; peer review emphasizes confidence in the tool's ability to uncover complex behaviors.

Complete agreement on GBM dataset application (C32-C35). Both evaluations support the findings and note consistency with original studies. OpenEval provides detailed figure references; peer review groups this with other validation datasets as evidence of the tool's capability.

Both support DMG behavioral clustering results (C36-C39). Peer review additionally includes C54-C55 (novelty of multiparametric approach), which OpenEval addresses separately in R9. Both emphasize the tool's ability to identify distinct behavioral patterns that would be challenging with single-parameter analysis.

Complete agreement on large-scale TME phenotyping results (C40-C44). Both evaluations support the linkage between behavioral clusters and microenvironmental niches. Peer review specifically highlights the CytoMAP combination as exciting and valuable for researchers.

Both support small-scale TME phenotyping findings (C45-C49). Peer review additionally covers C50-C53, C60-C61 (blood vessel and SR101+ associations), which OpenEval addresses separately in R7, R8, and R10. Peer review notes findings are preliminary but appropriately tempered; both find the spatial associations exciting.

OpenEval supports fast-migrating cells' association with blood vessels (C50-C51) with literature backing. Peer review groups this with other small-scale TME findings and accepts it as preliminary evidence that is appropriately presented.

OpenEval rates slow-retreating/SR101+ association (C52-C53) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative interpretation lacking direct validation. Peer review groups this with other TME findings and accepts it as preliminary evidence with appropriately tempered conclusions.

OpenEval supports the novelty and utility of multiparametric approach (C54-C56). Peer review addresses C54-C55 within the DMG clustering evaluation (R4), emphasizing how the tool reveals patterns challenging to identify with single parameters. Both agree on the value of this approach.

Both support the comparison between small-scale and large-scale TME phenotyping approaches (C58-C59). OpenEval also covers C60-C61 (novelty claims), which peer review addresses in R6. Both accept the interpretations as appropriately presented.

OpenEval supports the acknowledgment of limitations and literature-based justification (C62-C65). Peer review rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting the analysis provides only preliminary evidence but conclusions are appropriately tempered. Both recognize the need for further validation while accepting the current presentation.

Both address feature selection capabilities and limitations (C66-C67). OpenEval emphasizes the demonstrated capability and appropriate acknowledgment of noise potential. Peer review notes these as weaknesses regarding insufficient characterization of heterogeneity and cell-cell interactions, but accepts the tool's current scope.

Both support background claims about IVM capabilities and limitations (C1-C2, C11-C16). Peer review additionally covers C3, C17, C20-C21 (barriers to adoption), which OpenEval addresses separately in R18. Both accept the motivation and context for developing BEHAV3D-TP.

OpenEval supports claims about limitations of existing tools and barriers to adoption (C3, C20-C21). Peer review groups these with broader background claims in R10. Both accept these as valid motivation for the tool's accessible design.

Both support overall utility claims (C73). OpenEval also covers C69-C70 (Google Colab implementation), which peer review addresses in R1. Both affirm the tool's value and potential as an addition to researchers' toolboxes.

OpenEval supports computational methods in Heterogeneity module (C81-C86). Peer review groups these with other methodological details in R12, noting no concerns were raised about technical implementation. Both accept the methods as appropriate and well-documented.

OpenEval supports distance thresholds for Small-scale phenotyping (C87-C88). Peer review groups these with other methodological details in R12, accepting the technical implementation without concerns.

OpenEval supports statistical methods (C89-C92). Peer review groups these with other methodological details in R12, noting no concerns about the statistical approaches. Both accept the methods as appropriate for the experimental design.

OpenEval supports cell line authentication, ethical approvals, and reagent characterization (C74-C78). Peer review groups these with other methodological details in R12, accepting them as standard quality control measures without concerns.

OpenEval supports interpretations comparing TME approaches and novelty of SR101+ association (C60-C61). Peer review addresses these within small-scale TME findings (R6), accepting them as preliminary but appropriately presented evidence.

OpenEval supports interpretation regarding chemotactic cues (C56). Peer review addresses this in R8 as part of broader limitations discussion, noting conclusions are appropriately tempered. Both recognize the speculative nature while accepting the presentation.

OpenEval supports Google Colab implementation details (C69-C70). Peer review addresses these within the broader tool capabilities evaluation (R1), affirming the accessibility benefits. Both accept the platform choice and its implications.
